Subject: Renewal: staged GPU reserve increase and monthly commit cadence

Hi Jonathan —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Based on your usage patterns and the Q4 traffic forecast you shared, we put together a proposal to transition your dedicated pool from 8 → 16 GPUs during the upcoming renewal window while preserving cost predictability. High-level outline: 

- Phased activation: Add 4 GPUs in week 1 of the renewal month, +4 GPUs in week 3 (finalize by day 21).
- Monthly reserved commit: migrate from your current 8-GPU baseline to a 16-GPU baseline with a revised monthly commitment (see attached draft amendment). We included a two-month pro-rata adjustment for the phased activation.
- Throughput & fallbacks: prioritized routing to the 16-GPU pool with automatic fallback to compatible burst instances if regional capacity is constrained.
- Canary & activation window: 10–14 day canary with traffic targeting and rollback hooks.

Can you confirm your target go-live month (we assumed Nov 1) and whether a staggered activation works operationally? Also: do you have an updated peak concurrent inference jobs estimate or a preferred model family mix (gpt-4x-style vs. smaller Llama-family) so we can fine-tune kernels/quantization suggestions?

I attached a draft amendment and an SLA/RFP excerpt for quick review. If that timeline looks good we can produce a redlined amendment and start procurement timing.

—Alex

Hi Jonathan — appreciate the quick review. Answers below and a proposed commercial term you can share with procurement: 

- Commercials (proposal): move to a 16-GPU reserved pool with a revised monthly commitment of $98,500/month, effective at renewal; annual pay-in-full would unlock a 7.5% discount (optional). The attached Draft_Amendment_8to16.xlsx includes line-item prorate for November based on the phased activation schedule (first 4 GPUs active 11/01–11/14, remaining 4 active 11/15–11/21).
- SLA & throughput: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool measured monthly. Latency targets: p50 < 90ms and p95 < 180ms for 512-token inference on the recommended model family; we’ll include an SLO with automated failover to burst capacity (no data plane change required). If you have a specific percentile SLA request beyond that, we can discuss escalated SLA pricing.
- Procurement & timeline: we can deliver a redline-ready amendment and DocuSign package by EOD 10/05 to meet your 10/07 internal deadline.
- SOC2 and compliance: SOC2 Type II package and evidence URL included here: https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_Documents (I’ve flagged the SOC2 report for your security team).

Operational notes: we recommend running the canary against a 20% traffic slice and monitoring token-level cost and latency via Redwood Console dashboards; if you prefer, Ben can own the ops runbook and schedule the canary calls.

Next steps: I’ll prepare the amendment with the exact monthly figures and a short ops playbook. Please confirm acceptance of the $98,500/month baseline and the staged activation approach.

Thanks —
